results.newText: What % of pet owners talk to their pets like they're people?
results.reason: Preply surveyed 1,500 American dog and cat owners (July 2023): 84% regularly talk to their pets like fellow humans. The original wording ('people') has no matching stat, so the question is reframed to pet owners, the population actually measured.
results.source: Preply survey of 1,500 American pet owners, July 2023: 84% regularly talk to their pets like fellow humans

results.reason: YouGov (Oct 1-6, 2025, n=1,136 US adult citizens) found 16% had personally 'seen a spirit or ghost'. A later YouGov wave (Sept 25-28, 2026) found 19%; using the published YouGov article figure of 16%. Original 36% matches no sighting stat (it is close to the 38% who BELIEVE ghosts exist, a different question).
results.source: YouGov, Oct 2025: 16% of US adult citizens reported having seen a spirit or ghost

results.newText: What % of women over 50 will break a bone because of osteoporosis?
results.reason: No published stat exists for 'never broken a single bone' in the general population; lifetime fracture risk is only published split by sex/cause. Reframed to the closest real, published figure: the International Osteoporosis Foundation reports almost 1 in 2 women over 50 experience a fracture (osteoporotic).
results.source: International Osteoporosis Foundation survey via UCB (2024): almost one in two women after age 50 experienced a fracture

results.reason: Already validated per task brief: Polythelia case report, Annals of Obstetrics and Gynecology (2024), prevalence range 0.2%-5.6%; answer uses the low end of the published range. Corroborated by ScienceDirect's supernumerary-nipple overview (Mehes: 0.2% in a Hungarian neonate sample). Keep as the non-votable population stat.
results.source: Polythelia case report, Annals of Obstetrics and Gynecology (2024): supernumerary-nipple prevalence 0.2%-5.6%

results.reason: Build-A-Bear / Atomik Research survey of 2,000 adults found 40% of adults sleep with a stuffed animal; also reported by CNN (2025). Original 35% matches a UK hotel survey of British adults, not the US/general figure.
results.source: Build-A-Bear / Atomik Research survey of 2,000 adults: 40% sleep with a stuffed animal (reported by CNN, 2025)

results.reason: Talker Research survey of 2,000 US adults (Sept 17-22, 2025, for Avocado Green Mattress): 29% admitted they are still afraid of the dark (33% of men, 26% of women). No published source supports 15%.
results.source: Talker Research, Sept 2025 (n=2,000 US adults): 29% still afraid of the dark

results.reason: Stallman & Kohler meta-analysis of 51 studies (n=100,490), PLOS ONE 2016: estimated lifetime prevalence of sleepwalking 6.9% (95% CI 4.6%-10.3%), rounded to 7%. Note: a single US Stanford study reported 29.2% lifetime, but the 51-study meta-analysis is the stronger published figure; the paper itself cautions about risk of bias.
results.source: Stallman & Kohler (2016), PLOS ONE: lifetime prevalence of sleepwalking 6.9%

results.reason: Searched for published surveys on eating snow on purpose; found nothing citable. Only unsourced radio-trivia claims (a Facebook post claiming 80% of kids / 15% of adults ate snow, and an 11% winter-habit quiz with no source). No named survey, census, or study measures this. REMOVE.

Searched for a general-population stat on eating insects on purpose; none exists. Only regional entomophagy studies (e.g. 54.5% in Ebonyi State, Nigeria; 67% in Myanmar) that describe specific local populations, not 'people' generally, so none can back the question as worded. REMOVE.

Published literature consistently gives 20-30% of the general population for nail biting (Halteh et al. 2017, Journal of Dermatological Treatment; Lee & Lipner 2022). The current answer of 30% sits at the top of that published range, so it is kept as stated.
results.source: Halteh et al. (2017): onychophagia affects approximately 20-30% of the general population

results.reason: Popchips / Talker Research survey of 5,000 US adults (May 7-19, 2026, 100 per state): 60% keep secret snack stashes inside their homes. Original 55% has no source.
results.source: Popchips / Talker Research, May 2026 (n=5,000 US adults): 60% keep secret snack stashes at home

results.newText: What % of Americans keep cash at home as part of their savings?
results.reason: No published stat measures 'cash hidden somewhere in the home' as worded; figures conflict (Amex 2014: 29% of savers keep some cash at home, 53% of those in a secret spot; Piere: average $544 hidden). Reframed to the cleanest recent published figure: LendingTree/DepositAccounts survey (Feb 2026, n=2,000) found 27% of Americans keep cash at home as savings.
results.source: LendingTree / DepositAccounts survey, Feb 2026 (n=2,000 US consumers): 27% keep cash at home as savings

results.reason: OnePoll / Victorinox survey of 2,000 Americans: 11% have never travelled outside the state where they were born. Widely reported and consistent across write-ups; keep as stated.
results.source: OnePoll / Victorinox survey of 2,000 Americans: 11% have never travelled outside their birth state

results.reason: Searched for a primary survey behind '1 in 4 Americans have appeared on TV'. Only an unsourced trivia claim repeated on content-farm pages and a 2000 university newspaper clipping; no named pollster, sample, or year could be traced. Fails the bar. REMOVE.

Searched for a representative survey of Americans able to name all 50 states. None exists. The figures floating around are unrepresentative or unsourced: 45% of self-selected Sporcle players, 9% for naming them in alphabetical order (from a maths textbook problem), 3% from a BuzzFeed quiz claim. REMOVE.
UN World Population Prospects 2024 via Worldometer: Brazil's 2024 population 211,998,573 = 2.60% of world population (8.16bn). Original 3% was a rounded-up estimate.
results.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024 (Worldometer): Brazil = 2.60% of world population in 2024

results.reason: Searched Running USA, RunRepeat and marathon-participation literature. Only annual finisher counts exist (Running USA: ~475,000-525,000 US finishers/year); no published lifetime percentage of US adults who have ever finished a marathon. Best available are rough global estimates (0.6-1.0% of adults, Marathon Handbook) that are explicitly back-of-envelope, not a measured stat. REMOVE.

results.newText: What % of US adults hold a PhD?
results.reason: No reliable global PhD-holder percentage exists: published estimates conflict wildly (0.1%-0.15% of world population from headcount estimates vs 'around 1%' repeated in secondary sources). Reframed to the solid published figure: ~2% of US adults hold a doctoral/PhD degree (US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2022).
results.source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2022: ~2% of US adults hold a doctoral degree

results.reason: NMMA / US Coast Guard figures widely cited: 11.9% of US households own a recreational boat (~14.5 million households). Rounded to 12%. Original 9% has no source.
results.source: National Marine Manufacturers Association / US Coast Guard: 11.9% of US households own a recreational boat

results.reason: Computed from two published rates, as allowed: ~10% of people are left-handed (de Kovel et al. 2019) and 1-2% of the world has natural red hair; 10% x 2% = 0.2%. Independence assumed; no direct study of the overlap exists, so the answer is the top of the 0.1-0.2% computed range. Keep as stated.
results.source: Computed: ~10% left-handed (de Kovel et al. 2019) x ~2% red-haired = 0.2%

results.newText: What % of Iceland's population was not born in Iceland?
results.reason: As briefed, Iceland is ~0.005% of world population (UN WPP: ~399,000 of 8.3bn), below the 0.01% floor and never to be rounded up. Reframed to a different measurable Iceland stat in range: 25.1% of Iceland's residents were not native-born as of 2024 (UN/World Bank data), rounded to 25%.
results.source: UN / World Bank data via GeoRank: 25.1% of Iceland's population was not native-born (2024)

results.newText: What % of everyone who has ever been to space flew as a private citizen?
results.reason: As briefed, ~700 people have ever been to space out of 8.3bn = ~0.00001%, far below the 0.01% floor. Reframed to a measurable in-range space stat: ~120 private civilians have flown to space out of ~700 total spacefarers = ~17% (Space Daily, June 2026).
results.source: Space Daily, June 2026: ~120 private civilians of ~700 total people who have ever been to space = ~17%

results.reason: Calendar math, as allowed: a 4-year cycle has 1,461 days and only one is February 29, so 1/1461 = 0.068%, rounded to 0.07%. Keep as stated. (Real-world rate is slightly lower because births are sometimes scheduled away from Feb 29.)
results.source: Calendar math: 1 in 1,461 days is February 29 = 0.068%

results.reason: Published Western-population estimates for absolute pitch range 0.01%-0.07% (Frontiers in Neuroscience 2016, citing Bachem 0.01% and Profita & Bidder 0.07%); the classic '1 in 10,000' (Ward 1999) equals 0.01%. Keep at the low end of the published range. Caveat: no study has ever measured perfect pitch in a true general-population sample — all figures come from musicians/volunteers — so this is the weakest keep in the set.
results.source: Frontiers in Neuroscience (2016): absolute pitch prevalence in Western populations estimated 0.01%-0.07%; Ward (1999): 1 in 10,000

results.newText: What % of US households own a business jet?
results.reason: No published stat exists for 'US households own a private plane' as worded. Reframed to a computed figure from two published inputs: 26,670 business jets and turboprops on the FAA US register (Oct 2026) divided by 132.7 million US households (Census ACS 2024) = 0.020%. (Note: this counts jets only, not small piston planes, which is why the question is reworded to business jets.)
results.source: Computed: 26,670 business jets/turboprops on FAA register (Oct 2026) / 132.7M US households (Census ACS 2024) = 0.02%
